newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny sees Q2 below analysts' estimates.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny sees Q2 below analysts' estimates.

text.p: Allegheny Teledyne Inc said Monday that its second quarter earnings should exceed the $0.34 per share earned in the year ago period, but may not reach analysts' consensus estimate of $0.43 a share.
The company also said it is moving to divest eight non-strategic businesses.

"Flat-rolled results are running 20 to 25 percent behind the strong second quarter we had in 1996. After this quarter, the comparison should be more favorable," chairman Richard P. Simmons said in a statement. "Our other significant specialty metals businesses continue to do well in the second quarter. However, the total specialty metals segment may be somewhat lower than a year ago," he said.
Simmons said the company's aerospace and electronics, industrial, and consumer results "should beat, or at least match, last year's second quarter."
Simmons did not identify the units targeted for divestiture, but said the businesses account for about $200 million in revenue and about $15 million in annual operating profit.
It said its board recently approved the company's proposal to begin the initial stages of divesting the businesses and that it hopes to complete the divestitures by the end of the year.

"Our strategic plans also include acquisitions which fit our criteria to further strengthen our company's ability to compete," Simmons said. "I will be disappointed if we cannot make at least one strategic acquisition of material size this year."
